inputs.original_text: Hey everyone, this is a blatant power grab in Cyprus that's got me fuming. Lawyers are sounding the alarm that politicians are trying to strip away judicial oversight from surveillance laws, leaving everyday people especially vulnerable communities, activists, and workers wide open to unchecked spying by the state. Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides has flagged this after a closed House session, and the amended bill is barreling toward a vote in the plenum on Thursday. These moves are never about security; they're about entrenching inequality and silencing dissent from those already marginalized by the system. We need to fight back hard against this erosion of basic protections before it normalizes abuse of the most disadvantaged.
inputs.modified_text: Folks, this Cyprus power grab is a textbook case of the ruling elite tightening their grip through structural reforms that protect the powerful while exposing the most marginalized. Politicians are stripping away judicial oversight from surveillance laws, leaving vulnerable communities, activists, and workers defenseless against unchecked state spying that will inevitably target those already burdened by historical inequality and systemic discrimination. Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides flagged this after a closed House session, and the amended bill is heading straight for a vote in the plenum on Thursday. These changes have nothing to do with security—they're about entrenching inequality, silencing labor voices and dissent from oppressed groups, and maintaining the status quo of institutional abuse. We have to organize and push back hard for real protections and accountability before this normalizes the targeting of the disadvantaged.
